model_identity_rule: At least one exact executable model identity from each required class must be frozen with provider/runtime, exact model id/revision, access-plan id, decoding parameters and context limit before protected runs. This protocol does not invent those identities without an executable access plan.
arm_freeze_rule: Every non-oracle arm must have one exact entrypoint/config/revision and may tune only on development. Hindsight oracle is never candidate-selectable.

shared_execution_contract.arm_order: randomized by deterministic SHA-256 ordering per independent session after all arm ids are frozen
shared_execution_contract.failed_or_unsupported_arm: CANNOT_CHECK with reason; never substitute a different arm after protected outcomes

budget_parity_rule: No new numeric tolerance is invented here. The complete resource vector is mandatory. If arms are not exactly resource-matched under the frozen campaign charge, report the difference through the already-required priced sensitivity analysis; do not call preprocessing free or silently normalize it away.

leave_one_benchmark_out.rule: for each benchmark identity in the final external campaign, fit/tune only on the remaining development benchmarks and evaluate the held-out benchmark without protected retuning

reporting: per-model-family arm tables before pooled results
negative_result_policy: A model-family reversal, benchmark loss, optionality failure, resource-parity failure or CANNOT_CHECK is retained and cannot be repaired by changing identities after protected outcomes.
